title: Catalog screenflow journey and microcopy playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects a candidate screenflow, annotated wireframe descriptions, and microcopy drafts for three tightly related Console experiences: the Model Catalog browse/detail surfaces, the Create Endpoint flow, and the Model Version Pinning/rollout interaction.

TL;DR / design intent:
- Make discovery fast: catalog list should surface cost/latency profile, last-validated-eval, and compatible endpoint templates.
- Reduce cognitive load during endpoint creation by progressively disclosing advanced settings (quantization profile, KV cache retention, batching target).
- Pinning must be explicit, reversible, and visible in both endpoint settings and the model catalog listing.
- Microcopy should be short, action-oriented, and highlight safety/sla implications when relevant.

Who this is for:
- Primary: platform engineers and ML engineers creating endpoints for product teams.
- Secondary: SREs and support staff who need to audit rollouts and pin history.

Constraints / non-goals:
- This doc focuses on Console UX only; infra/placement of actual routing, autoscaler behavior, or billing calculations are out of scope.
- No final visual design — these are content/wireframe notes for handoff to design.

Personas and primary jobs-to-be-done:
- Priya (ML infra): needs to create a dedicated-friendly endpoint with predictable latency for a customer demo. Wants a quick way to pin a reproducible model version.
- Omar (Product dev): wants to test a new model variant behind a flag; prefers a canary rollout and easy rollback.

Overall screenflow (high level):
1) Catalog list (browse) -> 2) Model detail panel -> 3) Quick-create endpoint (lightbox) OR Full-create wizard -> 4) Endpoint settings page (post-create) -> 5) Pin version modal / rollout modal -> 6) Confirmation + audit trail entry

Annotated screens + microcopy (rough wireframe descriptions):
Screen 1: Catalog list (table / cards)
- Left: filter rail (tags: task type, architecture, quantization available, cpu/gpu).
- Center: card list showing name, flavor (gpt-3 style), short tags (latency tier, token cost tier), small metric chips (p50 p95 latency, tokens/sec), last validation date.
- Right: quick actions on each card: [Open detail], [Compare] (checkbox).
- Microcopy snippets:
  - Empty state: "No models match your filters. Try removing 'experimental' or expand the architecture filter."
  - Card subtitle: "Verified by Redwood — cost & latency profiles are estimates for {region}."

Screen 2: Model detail (slide-over)
- Top: model header (name + version dropdown + star/pin icon).
- Middle: summary row with: typical use cases, recommended endpoint template, sample prompt + sample tokens.
- Bottom: tabs: Performance, Compat & Artifacts, Eval results.
- Primary CTAs: [Create endpoint] (primary), [Pin this version] (secondary).
- Microcopy:
  - Recommended template explanation tooltip: "A starter config tuned for chat/turn-taking workloads. Adjust batching and latency SLO to optimize cost."
  - Pin CTA tooltip: "Pinning records this exact byte-for-byte model artifact for the endpoint. Unpinning will re-enable automatic upgrades."

Screen 3A: Quick-create endpoint (lightbox)
- Fields (condensed): Endpoint name (prefill: {model-name}-ep), Region, Template (dropdown), Capacity (small/medium/large), Public/private toggle.
- Expand link: "Show advanced settings" -> reveals quantization profile, batch target, KV cache policy, request-level timeout.
- Copy examples:
  - Name helper: "Use lowercase, alphanumeric and hyphens. Endpoint names are unique per org."
  - Capacity helper: "Estimated tokens/sec shown after selecting template."
  - Advanced setting hint: "Most demos are fine with default settings — open only if you need predictable p95 latency or lower cost."
- Confirm button: [Create endpoint — estimated cost: $0.12/hour] (button label should reflect selected capacity).

Screen 3B: Full-create wizard (multi-step) — for dedicated/private customers
- Step 1: Name & model selection (allow pick exact model:version).
- Step 2: Capacity & autoscaling (min/max, burst policy).
- Step 3: Security & network (VPC placement, encryption).
- Step 4: Pinning & rollout defaults (default model update policy: Auto/Notify/Manual).
- Microcopy:
  - Rollout default explanation: "Auto: endpoint will automatically receive minor model updates. Manual (pin): endpoint keeps current model until you explicitly update it."

Screen 4: Endpoint settings page (post-create)
- Prominent: current model pinned status chip (Pinned to v2.1) and small 'Modify pin' action.
- Left nav: Traffic & routing, Metrics, Versions & artifacts, Audit log, Edit settings.
- Versions & artifacts section shows available model versions, smoke-test pass/fail, created_at, artifact hash, and three actions beside each: [Promote to live], [Stage as canary], [Compare].
- Microcopy:
  - Promote tooltip: "Replace the endpoint's live model immediately. This action is logged and can be rolled back."
  - Canary tooltip: "Route a percentage of traffic to this version — metrics will show side-by-side comparisons."

Screen 5: Pin version modal / pin flow (critical copy and states)
- Modal header: "Pin model version to this endpoint"
- Primary body: short explanation + required confirmation checkbox if endpoint has > 1k TPS or is SLA-backed.
- Two radio options:
  - Keep current (Unpinned / Automatic updates) — description: "Endpoint will follow the recommended model updates unless you pin."
  - Pin to specific artifact (selected) — show artifact id, commit hash, eval summary.
- Warning block (only visible if the model has failing evals or incompatible features): red banner: "This version failed the regression suite on 3 prompts — pinning will prevent future fixes from being applied automatically."
- Buttons: [Pin version] (primary) and [Cancel] (secondary).
- Confirmation microcopy after success: "Pinned to vX.Y. Endpoint will remain on this artifact until you unpin or promote a new version."

Error & edge states (copy drafts):
- Failure to create endpoint due to quota:
  - Banner: "Insufficient capacity. This endpoint requires 2 GPUs in {region}. Request more capacity or choose a smaller profile."
- Conflict on pin (someone else changed pin during flow):
  - Inline: "Pin conflict: The endpoint was updated 12s ago by Jun Park. Review the latest pinned version or try again."
- Rollout blocked by failing smoke test:
  - CTA: "Confirm rollback" and small link: "View failing prompts"

Backlog grooming notes (tickets & acceptance criteria):
- RDW-1423: Catalog: show latency/cost chips in list view (5 pts)
  - ACs: chips display p50/p95 (ms) and token-cost-estimate (cent/token); regional toggle respected; clicking chip opens detail tooltip with sample histogram.
- RDW-1490: Pin modal + audit trail (8 pts)
  - ACs: pin modal shows artifact hash, optional confirmation checkbox for SLAs, post-action audit event visible in endpoint audit log with user/time/hash.
- RDW-1512: Canary rollout UI and percent selector (3 pts)
  - ACs: percent selector supports 0.1% granularity up to 10%, then 1% granularity; metrics show side-by-side for canary vs baseline for selected window.
- RDW-1533: Quick-create estimated cost calc (2 pts)
  - ACs: estimate shown within 2s after selecting template, uses cached cost table, falls back to note: 'estimate unavailable' if offline.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What level of artifact detail do Legal/compliance need on the pin modal? (hash vs full provenance link) -> Action: ask Security & Legal (Lina)
- Should the default on Quick-create template for Hosted API be 'Auto-update (recommended)' or 'Manual (pin recommended for production)'? 
  - Proposal: default to Auto for new users, Manual for enterprise orgs (detect via billing).
- UX for showing 'pinned because of SLA' vs 'pinned by user' — need distinct badges?

Design handoff checklist (for next step):
- Provide artboard for Catalog list with chip style + tooltip states.
- Annotated slide-over for model detail with exact copy strings.
- Pin modal states: normal, warning, conflict, success.
- Microcopy asset file: single source of truth JSON mapping copy keys to strings (for i18n).

Notes to PM / Eng:
- Implementation should emit audit events: pin.create, pin.remove, create.endpoint, endpoint.promote, endpoint.canary_adjust. Each event must include user, ts, artifact hash, endpoint id, and optional reason.
- For RDW-1423 implement a lightweight client-side cache for cost/latency chips to keep the catalog listing responsive. Put a 30s TTL.

Working TODOs (short):
- [ ] Confirm wording for SLA confirmation checkbox with Legal. (Owner: Lina)
- [ ] Create final microcopy JSON (Owner: Ava)
- [ ] Add canary percent selector component spec (Owner: Jun)
- [ ] Add product analytics to track pin/unpin events and conversion from quick-create to full-wizard (Owner: Marcus)

Draft change log:
- 2025-01-10: initial outline and first-pass microcopy (Ava)
- 2025-01-18: added backlog tickets and ACs after grooming (Jun)
- 2025-02-05: added canary notes and conflict states (Ava)

-- end --
